identity.name: TRANS & RECTI. LTD
identity.industry: Power Transformer & High-Voltage Grid Equipment Manufacturing (T&D capex play)

summary.oneLiner: a sharp deceleration vs peers doing 50, 28.

one-line thesis: A **deliberate air-pocket quarter**: revenue grew only +10% YoY (standalone INR559 cr) — a sharp deceleration vs peers doing 50–60% — because the Changodar plant is down for expansion/modernization (~27% utilization). Order engine is the real story: **UEOB INR6,630 cr (+26% YoY), Q1 inflow INR2,114 cr (+218%)** headlined by a **>INR1,000 cr PGCIL Ultra-Mega single-shot order**. Management held FY27 guidance (25% rev growth, 16% standalone / 20%+ consol EBITDA) with growth "picking up from Q3FY27" as Changodar restabilises and the INR900–1,000 cr backward-integration programme lands through FY27–28.
financial scorecard:
| Metric | Q1 FY27 Standalone | Q1 FY27 Consolidated | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | INR 559 cr (**+10% YoY**) | INR 572 cr | growth throttled by Changodar downtime, not demand |
| EBITDA | INR 87 cr (**margin 15.6%**) | INR 110 cr (**margin 19.2%**) | consol carries subsidiary benefit |
| PAT | INR 50 cr (margin 8.9%) | INR 64 cr | — |
| UEOB (order book) | **INR 6,630 cr** (+26% YoY) | — | executable over 18–24 months |
| Q1 order inflow | **INR 2,114 cr** (+218% YoY) | — | vs low base last year |
| Power-transformer order book | ~INR 5,300 cr | — | "fairly spread" 66kV–765kV |

**One-offs / adjustments:** (1) Employee cost fell to INR 22 cr (from INR 38 cr in Q4FY26) — prior quarter carried ESOP + MD-commission provisions; this quarter is the clean run-rate. (2) Other expenses ~12% of sales (vs usual 13–14%) — mgmt says no one-off (INR 66 cr vs INR 69.74 cr YoY). (3) **Inventory deliberately built high** (RM stocked through Dec-2026 as a geopolitical hedge) → temporarily elevated working capital/interest. (4) FY26 5-yr CAGR: revenue 27% / EBITDA 38% / PAT 101%; ROCE 19.1%, ROE 15.7% (FY26).
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **FY27 revenue growth: 25%** (standalone/transformer level).
- **FY27 EBITDA margin: 16%** standalone (incl. other income); **consolidated 20–21%+** (subsidiary adds ~100 bps over standalone; FY26 consol blended was 17.3%). **PAT margin 9–10%.**
- **Order inflow: ~30% growth** in both domestic and export markets FY27.
- **Growth "picks up from Q3FY27"** once Changodar stabilises (expansion complete **August 2026**).
- **Export capped at 10–15% of revenue** ("will not go beyond 15%") — US (up to 765kV, 20-yr track record), Americas, Australia focus.
- **$1 bn / ~INR 8,000 cr revenue by FY28–29** ("FY29 very achievable"); reframed down from INR 9,600 cr on rupee levels → ~INR 5,000–6,000 cr core capacity + ~INR 800–1,000 cr backward-integration third-party sales.
- **Backward integration: +200–300 bps margin from FY28**; 80–85% of RM in-house on completion.
- **Working capital target: 120–130 days** (from ~170 days FY26).
order book & pipeline:
- **UEOB INR 6,630 cr** (+26% YoY, 30-Jun-2026), 18–24 month execution window. Q1 inflow **INR 2,114 cr (+218% YoY)**.
- **Major Q1 wins:** PGCIL Ultra-Mega **>INR 1,000 cr** (various ratings, 30-month execution — an exceptional single-shot order, not the usual 18–24m); GETCO ~INR 228 cr; RRVPNL INR 175 cr; **PDC AK LPIV LLC (USA) export ~INR 150 cr**.
- **Inquiries under negotiation INR 23,000 cr**; historical win ratio 10–15%; bidding 80% domestic / 20% export; ~equal split govt / private-utility / industrial.
- Mgmt expects **more PGCIL Ultra-Mega orders** to keep flowing (multiple more PGCIL inquiries under negotiation). All India tenders are L1-basis.
segment / subsidiary:
- **Capacity 75,000 MVA+** across plants (mgmt figure); PPT per-plant: **Moraiya 40,000 / Changodar 35,000 / Odhav 22,000 MVA** ("current"). Supports INR 5,000–6,000 cr revenue medium-term. Immediate priority = utilization, not new capacity.
- **Utilization the swing factor:** Changodar ~27% now (expansion) → 60–65% FY27 → 80–85% FY28; **Moraiya only ~57–65%** (constrained by "geopolitical issues" in RM), target 80–85% by Q3FY27; **Odhav 100%**. Revenue mix this quarter skewed to 220/400/765kV (Changodar, which does <220kV, was down) — will re-broaden by Aug-end.
- **Consol > standalone margin (19.2% vs 15.6%)** — subsidiary contribution meaningful.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Backward integration (INR 900–1,000 cr)** — the twin cost-lever + independent revenue stream. Commissioning cadence: **CRGO already live**; **CTC Q2FY27**; **Pressboard Q3FY27**; **RIP bushings Q4FY27** (the "large bottleneck" currently); **Fabrication Q1FY28**. Third-party sales ~INR 800–1,000 cr (60–65% captive / 35–40% external).
- **HVDC:** ~**15–16 months** to full manufacturing; 9 months to finish the PGCIL repair job → PGCIL empanelment → first trial order. Design is **hybrid** (not pure LCC/VSC), treated as manufacturing secrecy; **no R&D capex currently**.
- **Emerging demand:** data centers, railway electrification, EV-charging, renewable integration all flagged as multi-year transformer-demand layers.
6a. moat & competitive position (optiona:
- **Backward integration as a structural edge:** in an industry where "component availability remains a key bottleneck globally," bringing 80–85% of RM in-house (CTC, bushings, pressboard, CRGO, fabrication) is positioned as a durable competitive advantage few peers have.
- **US EHV credibility:** "one of the big major suppliers up to 765 kV… track record of 765 kV transformers for more than 20 years" — qualification/track-record barrier in export EHV.
- **PGCIL trust:** a >INR 1,000 cr single-shot Ultra-Mega award (first of its kind for the company/industry per an analyst) signals top-tier utility confidence.
margins & cost dynamics:
- Standalone EBITDA 15.6%/guided 16% held **despite** an adverse mix quarter (heavy on lower-margin… actually higher-kV 220/400/765 this quarter) and Changodar downtime — mgmt insists margin will NOT fall to 14–15% when Changodar (lower-kV) returns because orders are protected.
- **Price-variation clauses** protect most orders; additionally RM stocked through Dec-2026 as a geopolitical hedge (double protection). Backward integration to add 200–300 bps from FY28.
- CRGO **anti-dumping investigation (DGTR)** a potential RM-cost risk — mgmt declined to comment, notes India's electricity-demand growth may force a relook; already inventory-protected.
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- **Changodar expansion (~INR 150 cr)** — delayed by extreme monsoon, labour constraints, engineering modifications; now on revised schedule, **complete by August 2026** (the single biggest near-term watch-item — it's the reason for the revenue air-pocket). **Moraiya expansion Q3FY27, on track.**
- Backward integration INR 900–1,000 cr; **finance-leasing ~INR 500 cr** of it, rest from ~INR 145–150 cr unutilised QIP + internal accruals → minimal fresh debt.
capital allocation:
- **Debt discipline:** standalone total debt ~INR 424 cr (FY26), D/E ~0.3x, Debt/EBITDA ~1.1x; mgmt "will not like to increase debt." Cash ~INR 139 cr + ~INR 145–150 cr earmarked QIP.
- Capex funded via QIP + leasing + accruals; **working-capital squeeze (170→120–130 days)** is the stated source of growth funding for the INR 6,630 cr book. No dividend/buyback discussed.
risks & watch-items:
- **Changodar downtime** is the dominant risk — it single-handedly capped growth at +10% while peers did 50–60%; Q3FY27 recovery is a mgmt promise, not yet delivered.
- **CRGO DGTR anti-dumping duty** — potential RM-cost inflation; unresolved.
- **Working-capital/inventory build** — deliberate RM stocking to Dec-2026 raises interest cost near-term; unwind depends on backward-integration coming online on time.
- **Guidance-vs-reality gap** — 25% FY27 growth needs a very strong H2 after a soft H1; $1bn/FY29 implies ~50% CAGR, reframed to ~INR 8,000 cr (analysts openly pressed the math).
- **Execution stacking** — five backward-integration plants + two capacity expansions + HVDC all commissioning across FY27–28; slippage risk is high (Changodar already slipped once).
- **Management change** — new CFO Mehul Shah; IR outsourced to EY (governance-signalling after prior-year churn).
management quality / tone: Confident, guidance-forward and unusually **disciplined on commitments** ("only those guidance parameters we are confident of achieving"). Candid that the +10% growth is self-inflicted (Changodar), repeatedly deflecting analyst probes on why utilization lags peers ("no major reason as such," "pretty much in line with market"). MD Mamtora crisp on HVDC/exports; CFO Mehul Shah detailed on balance sheet. EY-IR appointment + fast reporting framed as governance upgrades.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **This is a timing air-pocket, not a demand miss** — order book +26%, inflow +218%, INR 23,000 cr pipeline; the growth simply sits behind an August-2026 Changodar restart. The Q3FY27 inflection is the whole thesis.
- **The $1bn target quietly shrank** from INR 9,600 cr to ~INR 8,000 cr (rupee reframing) — a soft downgrade dressed as an FX technicality; watch whether even INR 8,000 cr by FY29 holds given a soft FY27 base (~INR 2,500 cr FY26 → needs huge FY28–29).
- **Backward integration is now a revenue line, not just a margin lever** — INR 800–1,000 cr third-party sales feed the top-line target, so its commissioning cadence (CTC→Pressboard→Bushing→Fabrication) is doubly load-bearing.
- **Inventory build is a strategic hedge, not distress** — RM secured to Dec-2026; the interest drag is a deliberate insurance premium against geopolitical/CRGO supply shocks.
- Consol margin (19.2%) already runs well above the 16% standalone guide — subsidiaries are the quiet margin engine.

themes.title: Transformer & grid-component shortage
themes.need: Transformer makers are running flat-out at record order books even as core-capacity ramps land (ATLANTAELE 16k->63k MVA, Q1FY27 record order book INR3,117cr on record INR972cr quarterly inflow, Vadod now PGCIL 400kV-approved with a 765kV tech tie-up in final talks; TARIL toward 75k+ MVA, Q1FY27 UEOB INR6,630cr +26% YoY on a >INR1,000cr single-shot PGCIL Ultra-Mega order, though a Changodar-expansion air-pocket held Q1 revenue to +10%; SHILCTECH adding 220kV) yet the binding constraint is still everything INSIDE a transformer - CRGO core steel, CTC/winding wire (KSHINTL/BHAGYANGR), bushings/insulators (YASHHV; 18-24mo lead, ~95% RIP/OIP imported) and transformer oil (APARINDS); both OEMs are now backward-integrating to own the bottleneck (TARIL's INR900-1,000cr CRGO/CTC/bushing/pressboard programme). Capacity-gated supply is the repeated 'need of the hour' and is driving pricing power now, though both OEMs flagged ~60,000 MVA of new 400kV capacity landing industry-wide in 3-4 months as a 1-year-out overcapacity watch-item (neither sees pricing pressure yet).
